title: Feb 2023 (Abu Dhabi)
des: DOH (HAAD) paediatrics recall, Abu Dhabi exam February 2023

questions.question: Atrioventricular septal defect is most commonly associated with which condition?
questions.exp: AVSD is the characteristic CHD of trisomy 21; all babies with Down syndrome need an echo.

questions.question: Polyhydramnios with a 'double bubble' on antenatal scan suggests which lesion?
questions.exp: High GI obstruction (oesophageal or duodenal atresia) causes polyhydramnios; duodenal atresia is associated with Down syndrome. Edwards syndrome also causes polyhydramnios.

questions.question: A child has a violaceous rash around the eyes, proximal myopathy and a raised CK. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Heliotrope rash, Gottron papules and proximal weakness with raised muscle enzymes = JDM.

questions.question: A well child suddenly develops a barking cough and stridor. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Croup (parainfluenza): coryza then barking cough, hoarse voice and inspiratory stridor in 6 months–3 years.

questions.question: A child has mild croup. What do you give?
questions.exp: All severities of croup benefit from a single dose of oral dexamethasone (0.15 mg/kg); mild croup can go home with advice.
questions.d: A single dose of oral dexamethasone and send home

questions.question: A child has moderate to severe stridor (adrenaline not offered as an option). What do you give?
questions.exp: Steroids reduce severity and admissions; nebulised adrenaline gives temporary relief in severe croup.

questions.question: A child has chickenpox. When can he return to nursery?
questions.exp: Exclude until all vesicles have crusted, usually 5 days after the rash.

questions.question: A child has a rash on the face and vesicles on the palms and soles. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Hand, foot and mouth disease.

questions.question: A 15-year-old with features of polycystic ovary syndrome has a normal oestradiol. What is the next step?
questions.exp: PCOS in adolescents needs hyperandrogenism (clinical or raised testosterone) plus irregular cycles; pelvic ultrasound is not recommended for diagnosis within 8 years of menarche.

questions.question: A child has periorbital cellulitis with normal eye movements. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Preseptal cellulitis in a well child: oral co-amoxiclav and close follow-up; IV if unwell or young.

questions.question: A child is brain dead; the parents do not agree to disconnect ventilation for 2 weeks. Which ethical principle is not being considered?
questions.exp: Continued intensive care after death uses resources others need (distributive justice); it offers no benefit and cannot harm the child.

questions.question: A child's mother died weeks ago. He is afraid of dying; his father is worried because he was fine before. What do you do?
questions.exp: Family-centred bereavement support first.
questions.b: Bereavement support for the whole family

questions.question: A boy took 30 paracetamol tablets over the past 12 hours. What is best?
questions.exp: Staggered overdoses cannot be plotted on the nomogram; treat with NAC straight away.
questions.c: Send a paracetamol level and start N-acetylcysteine immediately

questions.question: An infant arches and is irritable after each feed or within one hour. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: GOR with dystonic head, neck and trunk posturing; treat the reflux.

questions.question: A 3-day-old neonate on nasal CPAP suddenly develops tachypnoea and tachycardia. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: Sudden deterioration on CPAP suggests air leak; transilluminate and get a chest X-ray.

questions.question: A 2-year-old left alone suddenly started crying and coughing; he is now normal except reduced air entry on the right. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sudden choking episode then unilateral reduced air entry: rigid bronchoscopy.

questions.question: Trisomy 18 is associated with which feature?
questions.exp: Edwards: rocker-bottom feet, overlapping fingers, micrognathia, prominent occiput.

questions.question: A child has a red, swollen joint, cannot bear weight and has high fever. What is the management?
questions.exp: Septic arthritis: aspirate, culture, IV antibiotics ± surgical washout.

questions.question: A child has lymphadenopathy and pancytopenia. Which finding supports leukaemia?
questions.exp: High cell turnover raises urate and LDH; blasts on the film and bone marrow confirm.

questions.question: A child with likely IBD has a high faecal calprotectin and three bruises on the back. What do you check after admission?
questions.exp: Bruising suggests vitamin K malabsorption; check PT/INR.

questions.question: A patient has a prolonged bleeding time and reduced factor XIII. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Factor XIII deficiency gives normal PT, APTT and platelets with delayed bleeding; a prolonged bleeding time points to a platelet disorder such as Glanzmann. The recall was unsure.
questions.c: Factor XIII deficiency (with a platelet function problem if the bleeding time is prolonged)

questions.question: Which is NOT associated with Henoch–Schönlein purpura?
questions.exp: HSP has normal complement and platelets; it causes ileo-ileal intussusception and periarticular swelling.

questions.question: Which is NOT a feature of haemolytic uraemic syndrome?
questions.exp: HUS has thrombocytopenia, not thrombocytosis; leucocytosis and raised amylase (pancreatitis) can occur.

questions.question: Ostium primum ASD is associated with which finding?
questions.exp: Cleft mitral valve with regurgitation and left axis deviation.

questions.question: A 3-year-old is brought for tantrums and head banging, with morning vomiting and irritability. What do you do?
questions.exp: Morning vomiting and irritability suggest raised ICP: neuroimaging.

questions.question: A child has acute cerebellar ataxia after chickenpox; he is well apart from a wide-based gait. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Post-varicella cerebellitis resolves in weeks; image if atypical (reduced consciousness, focal signs).

questions.question: What is the EEG pattern in infantile spasms?
questions.exp: Hypsarrhythmia.

questions.question: Which statement about infantile spasms is NOT true?
questions.exp: Spasms peak at 3–8 months, not years. ACTH or prednisolone (and vigabatrin) are first-line; spasms are a feature of untreated PKU.
questions.b: They are a feature of untreated PKU

questions.question: A 6-month-old with bronchiolitis has RR 65 and SpO2 94% in air and is not feeding enough. How do you maintain hydration?
questions.exp: NICE: NG/OG feeds are first choice when oral intake is inadequate; IV fluids if NG not tolerated or impending respiratory failure.

questions.question: A child in respiratory distress: which blood gas finding is an indication for ventilation?
questions.exp: The recall marked PO2 <50. Persistent hypoxaemia despite high oxygen or PCO2 above 60 with acidosis are the usual triggers.

questions.question: Autism is suspected. After history, what is the best next step?
questions.exp: Exclude sensory impairment and refer for multidisciplinary developmental assessment.
questions.c: Hearing and vision assessment, then developmental assessment

questions.question: A girl has hallucinations of things creeping on her skin; GCS 15 and no focal signs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Psychiatric onset with normal GCS favours autoimmune (anti-NMDAR) encephalitis.

questions.question: A girl's height is on the 0.4th centile with features of Turner syndrome. What is the investigation?
questions.exp: Karyotype (30 cells to detect mosaicism).

questions.question: A 12-year-old girl with breast buds and pubic hair, not yet menstruating, has acne, abdominal striae and chin hair; weight 75th centile, height 25th. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Weight centile above height centile with striae and hirsutism suggests cortisol excess; check urinary free cortisol or late-night salivary cortisol. The recall was unsure between Cushing and PCOS.

questions.question: A 15-year-old athletic girl has stopped menstruating; pregnancy test is negative. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea from low energy availability; exclude pregnancy first.
questions.d: Relative energy deficiency in sport / anorexia nervosa

questions.question: A 4-month-old has fused cranial sutures and a small anterior fontanelle but is growing well. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Premature suture fusion gives an abnormal head shape and palpable ridge.

questions.question: Which syndrome is caused by a chromosomal deletion?
questions.exp: Cri du chat (5p deletion): high-pitched cry, microcephaly, learning disability. Trisomies are numerical anomalies.

questions.question: A neonate has poor feeding, hypotonia and small hands and feet. What is the future risk?
questions.exp: Prader–Willi: neonatal hypotonia and poor suck, then hyperphagia and obesity, hypogonadism and short stature.

questions.question: A 2-year-old with brittle hair has been licking tables and chairs (pica) since 4 months. What test helps?
questions.exp: Pica: check FBC, ferritin and lead.
questions.a: Blood lead level and iron studies

questions.question: What is the most common association of meconium aspiration?
questions.exp: PPHN.

questions.question: A newborn has cataract, heart murmur and hearing loss. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Rubella triad: cataract, PDA, deafness.

questions.question: A child has recurrent infections and cleft lip and palate. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: 22q11 deletion.

questions.question: A girl has ambiguous genitalia with hyperkalaemia and hyponatraemia. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency.

questions.question: How is congenital CMV diagnosed?
questions.exp: Urine or saliva PCR before 21 days; the main long-term sequela is sensorineural hearing loss.
questions.a: Urine PCR in the first 3 weeks

questions.question: A child has recurrent sinopulmonary infections, nasal polyps and situs inversus. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: PCD (Kartagener when situs inversus): neonatal respiratory distress, chronic wet cough, rhinosinusitis, otitis media. Diagnose with nasal nitric oxide and ciliary studies.

questions.question: A 2-year-old girl known to have asthma has repeated chest infections with minimal response to antibiotics. What is best to establish the diagnosis?
questions.exp: HRCT for suspected bronchiectasis.

questions.question: A 13-year-old girl has not had menarche; her mother had menarche at 15–16; bone age is 11.5 years. What do you do?
questions.exp: Delayed bone age with family history = constitutional delay; investigate primary amenorrhoea at 15.

questions.question: A child from Africa has haematuria and is otherwise healthy. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: Urinary schistosomiasis.

questions.question: A neglected child brought by a teacher and social worker has suprapubic pain, haematuria, fever 39 °C, proteinuria and nitrite-positive urine. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Fever, suprapubic pain and nitrite-positive urine = UTI.

questions.question: After 2 E. coli UTIs, a DMSA shows right 53% and left 47% with no scars. What do you do?
questions.exp: Normal split function (45–55%) without scars needs no follow-up.

questions.question: In a child with cerebral palsy, which finding should make you suspect abuse?
questions.exp: Bruising on protected areas.

questions.question: An infant has a spiral fracture of the humerus. What is the most likely explanation?
questions.exp: Spiral humeral fracture in a non-ambulant infant is highly suspicious of NAI.

questions.question: After a car accident a child lost consciousness, vomited and has a scalp haematoma over 6 cm. What do you do?
questions.exp: NICE: loss of consciousness with vomiting and a large haematoma require CT.

questions.question: A child has polyuria, polydipsia, headache and visual impairment (craniopharyngioma). What is the investigation?
questions.exp: MRI shows the suprasellar mass; then pituitary function and visual fields.

questions.question: Panhypopituitarism developed after treatment for medulloblastoma. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Cranial irradiation damages the hypothalamus/pituitary; spinal radiation affects spinal growth.

questions.question: What is used for congenital hypothyroidism screening in the UK?
questions.exp: UK blood spot screening uses TSH (misses central hypothyroidism).

questions.question: A 4-year-old with abdominal distension on laxatives without improvement now has more pain, a right hypochondrial mass and haematuria. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Flank mass with haematuria = Wilms tumour.

questions.question: A girl with hereditary spherocytosis has a recent drop in Hb with fatigue and poor appetite for a week. What is the most likely cause?
questions.exp: Parvovirus halts erythropoiesis; reticulocytes are low.

questions.question: Which statement about G6PD deficiency is correct?
questions.exp: Jaundice may indicate haemolysis. Quinolones and nitrofurantoin are oxidant risks.
questions.a: Nitrofurantoin can be given in breastfeeding of an affected baby

questions.question: A 13-year-old has deep sighing breathing and blood glucose 35 mmol/L. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Kussmaul breathing with hyperglycaemia.

questions.question: A girl in DKA has high glucose, pH 7.0 and bicarbonate 13. What is the best next step?
questions.exp: BSPED: fluids first; insulin infusion 1–2 hours after starting fluids; potassium added once K known and below 5.5.
questions.c: IV fluid bolus only, then insulin 1–2 hours later

questions.question: A stable child has SVT. What is the first treatment after vagal manoeuvres (ice to face, Valsalva)?
questions.exp: Adenosine.

questions.question: An 8-week-old has projectile vomiting after each feed (pyloric stenosis). What is the best initial management?
questions.exp: Correct hypochloraemic alkalosis and hypokalaemia first; pyloromyotomy is never an emergency.
questions.b: IV fluids to correct electrolytes before surgery

questions.question: A child has acanthosis nigricans. What is the next step?
questions.exp: Screen for insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes.

questions.question: A child has palpitations, weight loss and diarrhoea (typical hyperthyroidism). How is it diagnosed?
questions.exp: Suppressed TSH with raised free T4/T3, TRAb for Graves.
questions.c: Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4, T3) and TRAb

questions.question: A mother of three brings her 10-month-old who gained only 1 kg in the past 3 months; examination is normal. What do you do?
questions.exp: Weight gain slows to about 250–400 g/month at 6–12 months; 1 kg in 3 months is normal.

questions.question: A child has a triangular face, heart defect (peripheral pulmonary stenosis) and a history of cholestasis. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Alagille (JAG1).

questions.question: A child with type 1 diabetes should be screened yearly for which condition?
questions.exp: Annual TFT (and coeliac screening as indicated).

questions.question: In suspected physical abuse in an infant, what do you do?
questions.exp: Under 1 year: CT head, skeletal survey, retinal examination, bloods (FBC, coagulation, bone profile).
questions.a: Ophthalmology review, CT head and skeletal survey

questions.question: A child with bleeding has a mother with menorrhagia and a low factor VIII. What test confirms the diagnosis?
questions.exp: vWF antigen and activity (ristocetin cofactor); vWF carries factor VIII so it is low too.

questions.question: Which condition needs developmental follow-up?
questions.exp: HSV encephalitis causes long-term neurodevelopmental sequelae in many survivors.

questions.question: A 6-week-old has a rib fracture dated about 6 weeks; the mother says the baby was pulled and twisted during labour. What do you do?
questions.exp: Birth-related rib fractures are rare; full safeguarding work-up is needed.
questions.d: It might be NAI: admit for skeletal survey and child-protection assessment

questions.question: A neonate has features of Down syndrome. What is the best response?
questions.exp: Inform parents sensitively, confirm with karyotype (rapid FISH/QF-PCR), echo, and check red reflexes, thyroid and feeding.
questions.b: Senior review, talk to the parents, send karyotype and arrange an echo before discharge (or within 4 weeks)

questions.question: A child has tender red skin that peels, without mucosal involvement. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: SSSS spares mucosae; SJS/TEN involves them.

questions.question: A child from Africa has severe nappy dermatitis and failure to thrive. What should be supplied?
questions.exp: Acquired zinc deficiency.

questions.question: Which antiepileptic is most associated with agranulocytosis?
questions.exp: Carbamazepine causes leucopenia and rarely agranulocytosis; valproate causes thrombocytopenia and pancreatitis; lamotrigine rash.

questions.question: A girl on amitriptyline who 'usually lies' developed dizziness. What is the cause?
questions.exp: Tricyclic orthostatic hypotension; do not dismiss symptoms.

questions.question: A child has right arm and left leg weakness with normal examination. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Non-anatomical pattern.

questions.question: How is minimal change nephrotic syndrome treated?
questions.exp: Prednisolone 60 mg/m²/day for 4 weeks then alternate days for 4 weeks.

questions.question: What is true about puberty?
questions.exp: McCune–Albright causes peripheral precocious puberty.
questions.c: Pubic hair is the first sign in boys
questions.d: Menarche is the first sign in girls

questions.question: A very well child has visible haematuria 1–2 days after a URTI. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Synpharyngitic haematuria.
